A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConfTS research despite the changed title. All 24 pages of v2 and 27 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original calibration experiments, ConfTS image benchmarks, experiments combining ConfTS with ConfTr, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original image experiments and adds results for other calibrators, text classification, alternative loss functions and LAC prediction sets.

M1.justification: The core ConfTS loss, non-randomized APS score and validation-splitting procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.4 extends optimization from scalar temperature to Platt and vector-scaling parameters, introducing ConfPS and ConfVS as adaptations of the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds AG news and DBpedia text classification, substantially expanding beyond image classification. CIFAR-100, ImageNet and ImageNet-V2 remain covered. The new LAC experiments use retained classification coverage rather than introducing another task.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds comparisons involving ConfPS and ConfVS, while Table 4 evaluates ConfTr loss against ConfTS loss for temperature, Platt and vector scaling. The earlier comparison applying ConfTS to ConfTr-trained classifiers is removed; it is a different experiment, not a relocated version of the new loss comparison.

E3.justification: New text protocols use frozen BERT and GPT-Neo-1.3B encoders, trainable linear classifiers, AdamW, three epochs and equal calibration/test splits. SSCV evaluation is removed, and the motivation comparison narrows to ResNet50 on CIFAR-100. Its training instructions now reference batch size 128 rather than the 258 stated in v2 Appendix C; this establishes a reported setting change, not necessarily rerunning.

E4.justification: v3 adds LAC calibration and temperature-sensitivity analyses in Appendix E and the ConfTr-versus-ConfTS loss comparison. It removes the SSCV analysis and ConfTS-on-ConfTr experiment. The non-conformity-score ablation remains, while adaptiveness and validation/conformal-set-size analyses move to Appendices L–M without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the statement that experiments use 20 repetitions with different seeds. v3 removes significance markers and the two-sample t-test description from the retained main ImageNet Table 2, while corresponding statistical reporting remains in appendix benchmark tables.

E6.justification: v3 adds calibrator-extension, text, loss-comparison and LAC results, plus tuned temperatures, while removing ConfTr-combination, SSCV and several motivation-comparison results. Retained image benchmark rows largely match. Table 1 also reverses the reported CIFAR-100 ResNet50 TS/VS APS sizes: 7.35/6.69 in v2 versus 6.69/7.35 in v3. This is an unexplained reporting change, not an established performance gain.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1, Corollary 3.2, Theorem 3.3, the efficiency-gap definition, and their assumptions and proofs are retained after matching Appendix F to Appendix G. The generalized-calibrator equations reuse the existing softmax, APS score and loss construction rather than adding a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: v3 withdraws prominent claims of improved conditional coverage and benefits when combined with ConfTr-trained models. It adds claims about generalizing the loss to other calibrators, effectiveness in text classification including LLMs, and outperforming ConfTr loss. The central findings about confidence calibration and temperature remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly states that the findings do not generalize to LAC and that ConfTS may not improve conditional coverage, replacing v2's positive conditional-coverage interpretation and exchangeability-focused limitations paragraph. Appendix E interprets the new LAC evidence as lacking a consistent calibration–efficiency relationship. Section 3.3 also adds a rationale for preferring optimization over grid search for multi-parameter calibrators.

D1.justification: v3 documents text-classifier architecture, optimizer and training settings, and reports optimized temperatures in Table 2. Conversely, it omits the RTX 4090 hardware disclosure and the label-smoothing and mixup hyperparameter values previously supplied in v2. These are limited but concrete reproducibility-information changes.

R1.justification: The largely retained related-work survey moves to Appendix A. Its closest-work discussion replaces Gupta et al.'s binary-classification comparison with an explicit comparison to concurrent work by Dabah and Tirer, emphasizing broader calibration coverage and automatic optimization. References for text models, datasets and outlier detection are also added.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled Does confidence calibration improve conformal prediction?, with substantially rewritten abstract, introduction and conclusion and a new contribution list. The standalone Method section becomes Section 3.4, related work moves to Appendix A, and adaptiveness and dataset-size discussions move to Appendices L–M.

P2.justification: Table 1 consolidates earlier post-hoc and training-calibration displays, and Table 2 is reorganized with a temperature column. New comparison tables and LAC plots appear, the SSCV figure disappears, and the retained adaptiveness/size figure moves to the appendix. Typography, margins, author layout and table formatting also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The added calibrator comparisons, text experiments and LAC boundary analysis provide useful evidence, and conditional-coverage claims become more restrained. However, new central results contain unresolved reporting inconsistencies: Table 3 gives an APS baseline average of 13.890 although its eight entries average 6.945, and Table 4 reports 4.719 where the accompanying text gives 4.791. Main-table significance reporting is also reduced. These problems weaken confidence in the added evidence, leaving the net quality improvement uncertain.
